models.name: Airway-Scale Deposition CFD Model
models.what_it_computes: Transient airflow from oral cavity to segmental bronchi with polydisperse particle tracking to estimate regional and lobar deposition fractions, wall impaction hotspots, residence time distributions, and delivered lung dose.

models.name: Device–Mouth–Throat Jet CFD Model
models.what_it_computes: Device-resolved propellant jet, spacer flow, and mouth–throat transport using transient turbulence and evaporating droplets to compute entry-plane particle size–velocity–angle distributions and oropharyngeal deposition.

mechanisms.name: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High-velocity plumes increase oropharyngeal losses and reduce delivered lung dose; controlling impaction determines efficiency and local side-effect risk.

mechanisms.name: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Low-flow transport and pause enhance distal deposition of fine particles, affecting therapeutic reach to small airways.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported per model–mechanism pair on a 0–12 Depositional Credibility Index (DCI), with descriptive anchors at 0, 4, 8, and 12.

expected_decision.outcome_source: The present findings support the use of these models for mechanism-specific questions in pMDI–VHC design and usage guidance, with attention to the scope of each model.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
spans: Airflow boundary conditions for the airway model followed the coached adult profile described earlier.

The tracheal outlet split into lobar outlets with resistive elements tuned to match expected lobe flow distributions at steady 0.5 L/s inhalation based on morphometric ratios (right upper 16%, right middle 8%, right lower 26%, left upper 22%, left lower 28%).

Wall roughness was set to an equivalent sand-grain roughness of 30 micrometers in the mouth–throat and 15 micrometers in the tracheobronchial model, consistent with literature values for mucosal surfaces.
To bound albedo effects, a sensitivity case with half roughness produced a change in tracheal deposition below 0.2 percentage points.
findings.span: Airflow boundary conditions for the airway model followed the coached adult profile described earlier.

findings.mechanism: Jet-Driven Inertial Impaction During Actuation–Inhalation Overlap
spans: In the airway model, raising the inspiratory plateau to 0.8 L/s increased laryngeal plus tracheal deposition from 5.1% to 8.3% (+3.2 points) and reduced the median distal residence time by 0.4 s.
These runs use the same numerical settings as the nominal cases to isolate behavioral effects from numerical artifacts.
findings.span: In the airway model, raising the inspiratory plateau to 0.8 L/s increased laryngeal plus tracheal deposition from 5.1% to 8.3% (+3.2 points) and reduced the median distal residence time by 0.4 s.

findings.mechanism: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
findings.factor: Relevance of the quantities of interest
spans: The airway-scale model is aligned naturally with the breath-hold mechanism.
Its lobar fractions and residence times fall within expected physiological patterns and display low sensitivity to numerical settings.

The device-resolved model delivered a high-fidelity inlet SVA histogram (300 bins) and oropharyngeal loss estimate for the jet mechanism (DCI 12/12 for relevance), whereas the airway-scale model provided lobar shares and dwell times for the breath-hold mechanism (DCI 12/12 for relevance).
findings.span: The airway-scale model is aligned naturally with the breath-hold mechanism.

findings.mechanism: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
spans: During breath-hold, a low-level intrathoracic pressure decay of 25 Pa over 5 s was included to emulate glottis-open relaxation; sensitivity to this was negligible for the QOIs reported, with particle velocities below 0.01 m/s in segmental bronchi by 3.5 s.

findings.mechanism: Sedimentation and Diffusion During Post-Inhalation Breath-Hold
spans: Within the breath-hold mechanism, the airway model’s lobar fractions and residence times are sensitive primarily to particle size and the duration of the hold.
Reducing the hold to 0 s (i.e., no pause) yielded a delivered lung dose of 32.7% (1.2 points relative to 5 s), with a smaller distal share and a median distal residence time of 1.7 s.
Extending the hold to 10 s increased delivered lung dose to 34.8% (+0.9 points relative to 5 s), and lengthened the median dwell time by 0.7 s.
findings.span: Within the breath-hold mechanism, the airway model’s lobar fractions and residence times are sensitive primarily to particle size and the duration of the hold.

spans: In the device model, grid refinement from 60 million to 110 million control volumes reduced oropharyngeal deposition from 19.4% to 19.1% (0.3 points), while coarsening to 30 million increased it to 20.2% (+0.8 points).

Halving the time step cap during the actuation window from 10 microseconds to 5 microseconds altered oropharyngeal deposition from 19.4% to 19.3% (0.1 points), with no change in laryngeal fraction at the first decimal place.
